artifacts.summary: Measures the run-all.sh selection gap, re-measures the deployed-vs-source subject resolution ratio (52/91, down from 41/73 originally recorded), evaluates the naming-convention mapping's real coverage (identifying 18 core scripts with zero suite reference), and recommends a --only flag plus a grep-based suite-selection-lib.sh mapping.

memory_candidates.content: script-inventory.sh's has_test field resolves nested/flat test candidates against the CANDIDATE's own enclosing directory (e.g. scripts/lib/tests/test-X.sh), but this corpus's actual convention places all tests one level up in a single scripts/tests/ directory regardless of whether the subject lives in scripts/, scripts/lib/, or scripts/lint/. This means has_test under-reports lib/ and lint/ coverage for a reason distinct from (and more severe than) the basename-suffix caveat its own header already documents (lib/common.sh <-> test-common-lib.sh). Any future consumer of has_test for lib/ or lint/ candidates should verify this directory-resolution gap rather than trusting has_test: false as proof of missing coverage.

The prior Gate-8-parallelization task's deployed-vs-source subject resolution measurement (41 of 73 files preferring the deployed .claude/ copy) was produced by the exact command `grep -l '\$REPO_ROOT/\.claude' *.sh | wc -l` run inside agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/. Re-running this exact command is the correct way to get a comparable re-measurement over time; the ratio proved stable (56-57%) even as the suite count grew from 73 to 91, suggesting this is a structural corpus property, not a one-off artifact of a particular suite set.

In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/, a basename-convention touched-file-to-test mapping (test-<basename>.sh) is reliable for scripts/lint/*.sh (83% clean match) but unreliable for scripts/lib/*.sh and flat scripts/*.sh (35-41% clean match). The majority of the misses are not actually untested -- they are exercised by suites with non-matching names, often many-to-one (e.g. task-lookup-lib.sh is referenced by 20 different suites). A grep-based reference search (search every suite for the touched basename, not just a filename-convention check) finds a mapped suite for 85.6% of core's 125 non-test scripts; the remaining ~14% with zero reference anywhere is the real population that must trigger a fail-safe full-sweep escalation.
